title: Quantum dot synthesis uniformity for displays
bottleneck: Quantum dots give displays purer colors and better efficiency, but commercial value depends on size uniformity within a few percent — any spread broadens emission and washes out color. Batch synthesis inherently produces distributions that need wasteful purification, and continuous-flow reactors improve consistency but struggle with the core-shell structures that give dots their stability. Cadmium-free dots that match cadmium performance add another constraint.
why_it_blocks: Displays are a multi-hundred-billion-dollar market where quantum dots could cut power and improve color, but uniformity-limited yields keep costs high. The same synthesis problem blocks quantum dots in solar cells and medical imaging, where monodispersity matters even more.
current_state: Flow-chemistry production has improved batch-to-batch consistency for display-grade dots, and indium phosphide dots now serve the premium TV market. But cheap, perfectly uniform, heavy-metal-free quantum dots at commodity scale remain a process engineering challenge.
